title: Whole Milk 1 gal

drivers.name: Price increase (4.34 vs 4.16)
drivers.evidence: Same price last week sold 204 (x0.98 vs baseline); post-promo weeks average x0.96; noise-adjusted effect of price hikes is x0.96; one past price hike at same level observed.

adjustment.analysis: The baseline median is 207.3. The target week has no event or promotion, but a price increase to $4.34 (+4.3% vs regular $4.16). Historical data shows price hikes reduce demand: the week after a promotion (post-promotion effect) averages x0.85, and the noise-adjusted average for price increases is x0.96. The recent week with same price ($4.34) sold 204 units (x0.98 vs baseline), close to the noise-adjusted post-promo effect. No promotion is scheduled, so no uplift. The classical model’s x1.00 is unadjusted for price. Evidence is thin but consistent: price increase likely suppresses sales modestly.

KNOWN PLAN FOR THE TARGET WEEK:

  shelf price: 4.34 (+4.3% vs regular price 4.16)

STATISTICAL BASELINE (exponential smoothing of recent sales; it ignores events, promotions and prices):
  median 207.3 | 5%-95%: 166.4 - 327.6 | 10%-90%: 171.0 - 296.3

In the evidence below, 'vs baseline' = actual units / what this same baseline predicted for that week.
It is the multiplier that would have been right, so it maps directly onto median_multiplier.
This product's ordinary weeks already swing about +/-23% around the baseline, so a past effect smaller than that, seen only a few times, is mostly noise. The
'noise-adjusted estimate' is the effect shrunk toward x1.0 for that noise and the number of sightings.
